newsitem.title: USA: Minnesota corn 59 percent planted vs 9 week ago.
newsitem.headline: Minnesota corn 59 percent planted vs 9 week ago.

text.p: Minnesota farmers seeded half the intended corn acreage in the week ended Sunday as warmer temperatures dried fields and flood waters receded, according to the state's Agricultural Statistic Service.

Corn plantings were 59 percent complete as of Sunday, compared with nine percent last week and more than double the five-year average of 24 percent. Plantings were off to the fastest start since 1988.
"Crop producers took advantage of the excellent spring weather during the week and made great strides in field preparation and planting," the report said.
"In the portions of the Red River Valley watershed which were flooded, water is receding from cropland and farmsteads."
Soybeans were four percent seeded versus nil last week and the five-year average of three percent.
Spring wheat was 10 percent planted, trailing the average of 34 percent.
Sugarbeets were 30 percent planted, compared with the five-year average of 31 percent.
Soil moisture was rated three percent very short, nine percent short, 66 percent adequate and 22 percent surplus.
